about.title: Bell Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Bell sits along some of Los Angeles County's busiest surface streets and freeway stretches, and public records show 182 injury collisions and 249 injured people in the most recent final crash year. Florence Avenue, Gage Avenue, and the I-710 corridor see the heaviest reported volume, with Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up repeatedly in the data. Whether your crash happened at a Florence Avenue intersection, merging near I-710, or waiting at a light on Gage, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster you didn't ask for. We handle Bell car accident claims and can review what happened to explain your options. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and we work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government entity (like a city road or municipal vehicle) was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Means Every Percentage Counts
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your payout is reduced by your share of blame. Insurers often try to shift fault onto injured drivers early, which is why it helps to have someone reviewing the facts on your side.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, But No Recorded Statement Either
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but recorded statements to the other driver's insurer can be used to undercut your claim. We can advise you on what to say - and what to hold back - while evidence is still fresh.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Bell?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your accident involved a government vehicle or a hazard on a city-maintained road, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Saturday evening crashes seem common near Bell - does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: Public crash data shows Saturdays around 5-7 p.m. see more reported collisions in Bell, but timing alone doesn't determine fault or value. What matters is the specific facts of your crash - location, signals, speed, and evidence - which we can help gather while it's still available.

items.question: Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements to shift blame or minimize what they owe, and California's comparative fault rules mean even small admissions can affect your recovery.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a free case review?
items.answer: No. We offer free initial consultations, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
